question: When lava makes its way through cracks and fissures developed in the ground, it solidifies almost perpendicular to the ground. It cools down in the same position to develop a wall-like structure. What is this structure called?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dykes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dykes** are geological structures formed when magma intrudes into pre-existing rock formations and solidifies.
 
• They are generally **vertical or steeply inclined** and cut across the bedding planes of the host rock.
 
• Dykes often form **wall-like structures** that are perpendicular to the ground surface.
 
• These formations are important indicators of **tectonic activity** and magma movement within the Earth's crust.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lacolith:**

 
 
• A laccolith is a type of igneous intrusion that has a dome-shaped upper surface and a flat floor.
 
• It forms when magma intrudes between two layers of sedimentary rock, causing the overlying strata to bulge upwards.
 
• Laccoliths are typically smaller than batholiths and have a lens-like shape.
 
 
 
• **Lapolith:**
 
 
• A lapolith is a large, lenticular, igneous intrusion that is concave downward.
 
• It forms when magma intrudes into the crust and then spreads out laterally in a dome-like fashion.
 
• Lapoliths can be associated with large-scale volcanic activity and often contain significant mineral deposits.
 
 
 
• **Phacolith:**
 
 
• A phacolith is a lens-shaped igneous intrusion that is typically found in the cores of anticlines or the troughs of synclines.
 
• It forms when magma intrudes into the fold structures of sedimentary rocks.
 
• Phacoliths are usually smaller than laccoliths and are associated with fold mountain belts.
